# aeneid-085 — drafter's notes (XI.336–444)

45 units, 109 lines; `t` cut by `A.cut` in `make_units.py`; all script checks pass with no warnings.
Part name "The Quarrel of Drances and Turnus (XI.336–444)"; Latin title "Drances et Turnus. Altercatio".

## Speech marks
- Drances' speech: opens 343 (unit 343), closes 375 (unit 373). Turnus's: opens 378 (unit 377), closes 444
  (unit 442). l and i carry “ ” exactly where t does.
- 399 `“Nulla salus bello.`: the print opens a quotation and never closes it (presumably a nested `<q>` in the
  Perseus TEI that runs to the end of the speech, as at 084's 252/295). Turnus is quoting Drances' words of 362.
  Made its own unit; l/i put only those words in single marks (‘No safety in war.’ / ‘There is no safety in
  war,’ you say.). Note opens "The print has an opening double mark before 'Nulla' and no closing mark…".
  Treated as a quotation-marking decision, not a correction of the text.
- 442 `“devovi.`: stray opening mark, no speech begins; treated under rule 5b, omitted in l/i; the note of
  unit 440 opens "The print has an opening double mark before 'devovi', a stray mark…".
- EXEMPT = {399, 440} in the script (ln of the units concerned). Note: two units start at 399 ('Nulla salus
  bello.' and 'Capiti cane…'); the exemption covers both, but the second has no marks.

## Doubtful readings kept as printed
- 413 `regressum?` + lowercase `oremus`: not treated as a misprint. The three si-clauses (411–413) are read as
  rising to an indignant question; 411–414 kept as one unit so the '?' is internal; l/i keep the '?' and add a
  dash before "let us…". Note explains. A reviewer may prefer rule 5b (comma, as most modern texts punctuate).
- 425 `variisque` (Latin Library `variique`): hard to construe; kept as printed, l renders "with varied (turns)";
  note says the sense is the same either way. Could arguably be a Perseus/print slip for `variusque`/`variique`;
  I did not judge it a clear misprint.
- 378 `semper` position (Latin Library puts it before `Drance`): no change of sense; one sentence in the note.
- 367 `ingentis` taken with `agros` (et postponed), not with `funera` (neuter) — standard view as I recall it.
